title: Steps with Se, Results with Estar

sections.content: You know *se* with things from B1 Unit 6, the choice between passive and impersonal *se* from B2 Unit 19, and the state passive with *estar* from B2 Unit 20. A method or a popular-science explanation uses them as a pair. *Se* + a verb narrates the steps and keeps the person out of sight: the thing is the subject, so the verb agrees with it (*Se mezclan los ingredientes.*). *Estar* + a participle shows the state a step leaves, and the participle agrees with the thing like an adjective (*Los ingredientes están mezclados.*). So *se* says what is done, and *estar* says how things are now.

sections.title: The step and the result
rows: The dough is prepared. (the step: what is done)
The dough is prepared. (the result: how it is now)

items.spanish: Se pesa la harina y se añade la levadura.
items.english: The flour is weighed and the yeast is added.

items.spanish: Se mide la temperatura del agua.
items.english: The temperature of the water is measured.

items.spanish: Cuando la masa está mezclada, se deja reposar.
items.english: When the dough is mixed, it is left to rest.

items.spanish: Se miden las sustancias en un recipiente cerrado.
items.english: The substances are measured in a closed container.

sections.content: English says *is mixed* for both the step and the result. In Spanish, decide which one you mean: the action (*se mezcla*) or the state (*está mezclada*). Then check the agreement. After *se*, a plural thing needs a plural verb (*se miden las sustancias*, not *se mide las sustancias*). After *estar*, the participle agrees in gender and number (*las sustancias están medidas*).
